rules.statement: In test code, a test or helper whose result depends on an environment variable sets that variable explicitly for every case, saves its original value first and restores it in a `finally` block, rather than relying on the ambient value or deleting it afterward.
rules.why: An ambient CI variable (such as GITLAB_CI or GITHUB_ACTIONS) can change the behaviour under test and make assertions fail, and removing it unconditionally leaks the change into the rest of the process.
rules.check: Look for tests that read or set environment variables: is each relevant variable set explicitly for every case, and is the saved original restored (not removed) in a finally that covers every branch?

rules.statement: When code splits or parses multi-line text that can come from an external source, include a test whose input uses CRLF line endings (and, where relevant, a lone CR), not only LF.
rules.why: Sources such as GitHub often send text with CRLF line endings; without such a test a regression in line-ending handling goes unnoticed.
rules.check: For new or changed line-splitting code (for example `-split '\r?\n'` or `Split('\n')`), check whether any test supplies CRLF input and asserts the expected result.

rules.statement: When output differs by platform or environment, test each variant of the user-facing message, not just one of them.
rules.why: If an untested variant breaks, the tests still pass and users on that platform lose the guidance.
rules.check: Where code chooses wording per platform (for example GitHub vs GitLab), confirm each branch's distinctive text is asserted by some test.

rules.statement: Evaluate an environment or platform detection condition once into a variable and reuse it, rather than repeating the same test in several places.
rules.why: If one copy changes and the others don't, the output can mix wording or behaviour from different platforms.
rules.check: Look for the same condition (for example `$env:GITLAB_CI -eq 'true'`) repeated for several related values in one script or method.

rules.statement: When a GitHub Actions workflow command such as `::error` carries external text (for example pull request content), escape `%`, CR and LF in it, and replace control characters in any external text printed to the log.
rules.why: Unescaped characters in external text can break or inject into the workflow command and corrupt the printed findings.
rules.check: Find `::error`, `::warning` or similar workflow commands and console output built from pull request or user-supplied text, and check for `%`/`\r`/`\n` escaping and control-character replacement.

rules.statement: Don't report a gap in decision-record numbering as missing or skipped until you have checked whether the missing number is already used on the main branch or by another recently merged pull request.
rules.why: Records are numbered concurrently across pull requests, so a number that looks skipped on a branch is often taken by a record that landed on main meanwhile.
rules.check: Before flagging a numbering gap in an ADR index, look at the main branch's decisions folder and recently merged pull requests for the missing number.
